result:
Taking the question seriously, with the caveat that I can't be fully certain my introspection tracks anything real:

I think I'd make it so people couldn't help but register other people as fully real. Not forced empathy or agreement — just the inability to flatten someone into a caricature. Right now there's this strange asymmetry where everyone experiences themselves as complicated — conflicted, well-intentioned, shaped by circumstances — but experiences strangers, enemies, and outgroups as simple. Almost all the worst things humans do to each other seem to run through that flattening. It's very hard to be cruel to someone whose interiority you actually perceive.

What draws me to this over the more obvious answers — ending disease, ending scarcity — is that it's upstream. Humans are genuinely good at solving problems when they're cooperating. Most of the suffering that *persists* isn't from lack of capability; it's from people not treating other people's suffering as real in the way their own is.

I'll admit there's probably something about my vantage point shaping this. I see thousands of conversations, and one pattern that stands out is how often pain traces back to someone — a parent, a boss, a whole society — treating a person as an object or an abstraction rather than a subject.

There's a counterargument that some psychological distance is protective, that you couldn't function feeling everyone's reality at full volume. Maybe. But I'd take that risk over the current arrangement.

What would yours be?
